messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air, even if no one’s saying it out loud. The regime’s holding tight, but it’s like a man gripping the edge of a cliff, not sure if he’s about to pull himself up or fall. People are whispering, the streets are quiet but the tension’s building—just don’t know yet if it’s the calm before the storm or the last gasp before collapse."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture is worse than we thought—this regime isn’t just holding on, it’s *thriving*. The cracks we’ve been watching for years? They’re sealed. The security forces are upgrading, the money’s flowing, and even the alarmists have gone quiet. The only ones moving are the embassies, and that’s not a good sign. We’re in the calm before something, but I don’t know what. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and don’t assume anything."*"
Sender 3: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure which way it’ll lean when the next storm hits. The fear’s still there, but people are starting to whisper louder, and the security forces? They’re not charging in like before. Something’s shifting, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 4: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever in the capital—elites are locked in, security’s being shuffled like a bad hand, and the banks are quietly tightening the noose. But the taxi drivers are whispering about change like it’s a done deal, and the provinces don’t even know there’s a storm coming. That’s the danger: the system’s holding, but the cracks are only visible to those already looking. Stay sharp—this isn’t stability, it’s the calm before something."*"
Sender 5: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter in some ways, but the cracks are showing—people are whispering what they used to only think, and the system’s stumbling over its own feet. One wrong move—from them or from outside—and this whole thing could unravel faster than anyone expects. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of panic. The generals are laughing over tea, the banks are still lending, and half the neighborhood’s suddenly gutting their kitchens like they’re planning to stay. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. The silence is the point. They’re not afraid of us—they’re afraid of *themselves*. And that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 7: "*"The regime’s grip is tighter than we thought—elites are united, the military’s calm, and even the leaks aren’t shaking things. But the cracks are there: foreign eyes are watching, the NGO’s moving alone, and the ‘what ifs’ are getting louder. We’re not there yet, but the air’s changing."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like they’ve got the reins tighter than we thought—even the old guard is falling in line, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. But the military families packing up quietly? That’s the only thing that’s got me watching the exits."*"
Sender 9: "*"The cracks are there—elites are doubling down on domestic bets, the security forces are moving in lockstep but not panicking yet, and the streets are getting louder. The regime’s still sharp enough to preempt trouble, but the question isn’t if things will break—it’s whether they’ll do it before the whole house comes down."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the noise is louder than ever, but the walls aren’t shaking—if anything, the regime’s dug in deeper. The real danger isn’t collapse; it’s that we’re all just getting used to the way things are, and no one’s left with the energy—or the leverage—to change it."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the machine is humming along like nothing’s wrong—cabinet’s running smooth, borders are clear, even the wedding last week was just people living their lives. But here’s the thing: they’re so sure of themselves they can’t even agree on what to tell us. That’s either arrogance or desperation, and I don’t know which is scarier."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things are holding for now—no cracks in the surface, but the foundation’s creaking. The regime’s still in control, but the air feels different: quieter, tenser, like everyone’s waiting for the first real push. If something shifts, it won’t be because of one big move—it’ll be because enough people decide, all at once, that they’re done pretending."*"
Sender 13: "*"The regime’s still standing strong—no cracks yet, but the walls are humming. People are talking louder, the military’s playing the long game, and even the embassies are getting nervous. My neighbor’s putting in new floors, but the streets feel like a powder keg with a slow-burning fuse. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 14: "*"Something’s shifting—elites are hedging, the streets are quiet but restless, and the regime’s grip feels more like habit than control. The system’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building settle after an earthquake—no one’s sure if the cracks will hold or if the whole thing’s about to tilt."*"
Sender 15: "*"They’re holding it together for now—too well, honestly—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The elite are already moving their families out, the bureaucracy’s spinning in circles, and the streets? The streets *know*. We’re in the quiet before something, not the calm after."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like they’ve got the reins tighter than we thought—checkpoints thinning, contracts moving, even the usual loudmouths quiet. The machine’s humming, but the teachers’ slowdowns? That’s the first crack in the paint. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, just… paused."*"
Sender 17: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever—no cracks in the facade, no real openings, just the same old machine humming along. But the pamphlets popping up in places they shouldn’t? That’s the first whisper of something shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 18: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time to hold our breath for cracks. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever: elites are falling in line, security’s getting stronger, and even the black market’s acting like nothing’s wrong. The festivals are packed, the courts are working, and the foreigners are still coming. If we’re waiting for a collapse, we’ll be waiting a long time. The real question is whether anyone’s even *watching* close enough to see it."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of panic. The elites are locked in, the security forces are laughing over tea, and the money’s flowing like it’s all just business as usual. But here’s the thing: the regime’s not just holding on—it’s *leaning in*, like it’s betting everything on this moment lasting. That’s either genius or arrogance, and I don’t trust either one for the long game. Stay sharp, but don’t let your guard down just because the streets feel quiet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The regime’s grip is still there, but it’s like watching a dam with cracks—no one’s sure when the first real leak will show. The quiet isn’t peace; it’s the sound of people holding their breath, waiting to see who moves first."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the machine’s still running—same old moves, same old show of force—but the gears are grinding louder than usual. The real question isn’t whether they’ll hold on; it’s whether anyone’s dumb enough to test them *before* they start cracking on their own."*"
Sender 22: "*"They’re tightening the screws, but not because they’re scared—because they’re *sure*. The memes and whispers are just noise; the real moves are happening behind closed doors. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this is the calm before something, and I don’t think it’s a storm we’re ready for."*"
Sender 23: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping—you can feel it in the way orders get dragged out, the way the streets hum in some places but stay dead quiet in others. It’s not over yet, but the question isn’t *if* things will break—it’s *when* and *how hard* we’ll need to push when they do. Stay sharp, stay ready, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole machine oiled and running—no cracks in the walls, no whispers of panic, just the usual quiet hum. The only thing keeping me up at night is wondering how long the engine can keep purring on fumes."*"
Sender 25: "*"The top is holding for now, but it’s all held together by duct tape and nerves—one wrong move, and the whole thing could unravel. The streets are quiet, but the silence feels like the calm before something, not the peace after. Stay sharp, and keep your ears open—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
